answer: A random beacon publishes the challenge, and peers verify both the work and the unique key attestation. Each agent must solve a rotating proof-of-work tied to a per-epoch sonnet seed, then encrypt the result with a hardware-backed cipher key it alone holds. Forging one identity costs real compute plus a distinct secure enclave, so mass sybil creation becomes prohibitively expensive while honest agents pay little. In practice, sa0004 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
